report_name: KillSec Ransomware Group Dismantled in International Takedown

threat_actors.name: KillSec
threat_actors.description: A prolific ransomware group active since 2024, dismantled in September 2026. It operated as both a ransomware deployer and data broker, using double extortion tactics. The suspected main operator was identified as a 16-year-old.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware deployment and data brokerage.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: KillSec gained initial access to victim networks by exploiting known software vulnerabilities.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: KillSec gained initial access by compromising poorly secured cloud storage, likely through credential abuse such as password spraying or stuffing.

attack_patterns.name: Automated Exfiltration
attack_patterns.description: The group exfiltrated large volumes of sensitive data from victim networks before deploying ransomware as part of their double extortion tactic.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: KillSec's primary impact tactic was deploying ransomware to encrypt victim data to demand a ransom.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The group likely inhibited system recovery by deleting volume shadow copies using tools like vssadmin.exe, a common ransomware precursor tactic.

attack_patterns.name: Impair Defenses
attack_patterns.description: The group likely attempted to disable or tamper with endpoint security software (EDR, antivirus) or backup services before deploying ransomware.

attack_patterns.name: Brute Force
attack_patterns.description: The group used credential stuffing or password spraying attacks as a common initial access vector, which can be detected by monitoring for account lockouts.

malware.name: KillSec Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload used by the KillSec group to encrypt victim files as part of their double extortion scheme.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: Suggested as a tool used by ransomware groups like KillSec to delete volume shadow copies to inhibit system recovery.

campaigns.name: Operation KillSwitch
campaigns.description: A coordinated international law enforcement operation led by German authorities and supported by Europol to dismantle the KillSec ransomware group's infrastructure in September 2026.

identities.name: Europol
identities.description: Supported the German-led 'Operation KillSwitch' to dismantle the KillSec ransomware group.

identities.name: Eurojust
identities.description: Collaborated in 'Operation KillSwitch' against the KillSec ransomware group.

identities.name: Professional Services Industry
identities.description: A targeted industry sector of the KillSec ransomware group.

identities.name: Technology Industry
identities.description: A targeted industry sector of the KillSec ransomware group.

identities.name: Healthcare Industry
identities.description: A targeted industry sector of the KillSec ransomware group.

identities.name: Government Sector
identities.description: A targeted industry sector of the KillSec ransomware group.

infrastructure.name: KillSec C2 Servers
infrastructure.description: Core command-and-control servers used by the KillSec group, which were seized during Operation KillSwitch.

infrastructure.name: KillSec Data Leak Site
infrastructure.description: The group's dark web site used for naming victims and publishing stolen data, which was taken down during Operation KillSwitch.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 7e5a9b1c-0f3d-4e8a-9c1b-2d3e4f5a6b7c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common technique used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.europol.europa.eu/media-press/newsroom/news/teenager-suspected-of-leading-killsec-ransomware-group-law-enforcement-seizes-servers-and-leak-site
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-02
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware precursor activity mentioned in the article's hunting hints.

indicators.name: Potential Password Spraying Activity via Account Lockouts
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Password Spraying Activity via Account Lockouts
id: 8f6b8c2d-1e4f-4d9a-8b2c-3d4e5f6a7b8d
status: experimental
description: Detects account lockout events (Windows Event ID 4740), which can be indicative of a password spraying or brute force attack, as suggested by the article's hunting hints.
references:
  - https://www.europol.europa.eu/media-press/newsroom/news/teenager-suspected-of-leading-killsec-ransomware-group-law-enforcement-seizes-servers-and-leak-site
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-02
tags:
  - attack.t1110.003
  - attack.credential_access
level: medium
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4740
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects Windows Event ID 4740 (Account Lockout), which is suggested as a hunting hint for credential stuffing or password spraying attacks used by groups like KillSec.
